name: Drought
value: Sudan harvest hit; no famine declared
summary: El Niño drought cuts Sudan's harvest and raises famine risk; no new famine declaration or exporter harvest failure found
state: An IPC alert in mid-October warned that El Niño-driven drought on top of conflict raises famine risk in parts of Darfur and Kordofan, with poor harvests expected (Ahram Online, 12 Oct). Sudan's July–September rains were the lowest in more than three decades, and some farmers in Gedaref and North Kordofan expected about a quarter of normal yields (Reuters via TimesLIVE, 23 Oct). Severe drought in a major crop region keeps this at Watch; searches on 14 Nov found no new drought-driven famine declaration or major exporter harvest failure.
for_you: Most exposed are people in Darfur and Kordofan who depend on rain-fed harvests and aid. For other readers, effects tend to show up through humanitarian appeals and regional food prices rather than global grain supply.
rubric_hit: Severe drought in a major crop region (Sudan, rains lowest in 30+ years): Watch line; no famine declaration

sources.title: Ahram Online — Sudan's famine risk worsened by conflict, drought and funding shortages: Report
TimesLIVE (Reuters) — New famine risk haunts war-torn Sudan with El Niño-driven drought

why: Drought slowly destroys harvests, hydropower and river shipping, and drives famine and migration.
drivers: Rainfall deficits, heat, ENSO, groundwater depletion.

rubric.alert: Drought driving famine conditions, a major exporter's harvest failure, or monsoon failure across a major breadbasket.
rubric.watch: Severe drought in a major crop region, a major river at record low, or a monsoon running more than 20% below normal.
rubric.normal: No major breadbasket in severe drought.
